decisions.reason: Legal-document access is established by the separate footer-links clause and is already fully captured by its message-56 INTRODUCE; the Sign In styling change adds nothing further.
Using the landing-page background as a basis for Cognito styling does not change the landing page's own visual-system requirements.
The informational Sign In and provisioning-page styling decision does not modify the independently scoped console shell.
The broad shared-header-and-footer rule gains a necessary exception: the Sign In and Account Provisioning wizard pages require only a background and header logo, with footer inclusion optional.

Creation and styling of a Sign In page does not alter the landing-page sign-up button or its action.
The source does not change responsive behavior for the landing page.
The source does not change which marketing copy or sections belong on the landing page.
Reusing the landing-page background for Cognito styling does not change the required design-system tokens, font files, metadata, or content-width specification.
